# EDI: Experimental Design and Inference

> EDI (Experimental Design and Inference) is an R package that marries
> randomized experimental designs — fixed (block, stratified, matched-pair,
> cluster, factorial, rerandomization, and MILP-based optimal designs) and
> sequential (matching-on-the-fly and covariate-adaptive designs: Atkinson,
> Efron, Pocock-Simon, urn) — with inference procedures (exact, asymptotic,
> distribution-free, and resampling-based) matched to each design and
> response type: continuous, incidence (binary), count, proportion, survival
> with censoring, and ordinal. Core estimation kernels are C++ (Eigen +
> LBFGS++). Not related to Electronic Data Interchange.

Key facts:

- Typical workflow: construct an R6 design object (e.g. `DesignSeqOneByOneKK21`,
  `DesignFixedBlocking`), assign treatments (all at once for fixed designs,
  one subject at a time for sequential designs), record responses, then run a
  matched inference class (e.g. `InferenceContinKKOLSIVWC`) or `InferenceSuite`,
  which runs every applicable procedure and reports one Cauchy-combined p-value.
- A built-in `SimulationFramework` supports power analysis and
  operating-characteristic studies across designs, response types, and
  inference procedures, with optional parallelization via `mirai`.
- The distinct Python package `edi_kernels` (PyPI) exposes the same C++
  model-fitting kernels with no R dependency.

## Documentation

- [Function and class reference](https://kapelner.github.io/EDI/reference/index.html):
  every design class, inference class, and C++ backend kernel
- [Notation glossary](https://kapelner.github.io/EDI/articles/notation-glossary.html)
- [Reproducibility: RNG and seed conventions](https://kapelner.github.io/EDI/articles/reproducibility.html)
- [Backend contracts: fast_* C++ kernels](https://kapelner.github.io/EDI/articles/backend-contracts.html)
- [Validation evidence](https://kapelner.github.io/EDI/articles/validation-evidence.html)
- [Extending EDI with your own inference and design classes](https://kapelner.github.io/EDI/articles/extending-edi.html)

## Source and packages

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/kapelner/EDI): R package under
  `R/EDI`, Python package under `python`
- [Python package edi_kernels on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/edi_kernels/)
- [Issue tracker](https://github.com/kapelner/EDI/issues)
